title: Launchpad messaging and pricing hypotheses
content:
Context:
This doc is a compact ideation + hypothesis set for a developer-focused launch flow we're calling "Launchpad" — a minimal onramp for engineers evaluating Redwood Hosted endpoints. Goal: reduce time-to-first-success, make pricing and performance expectations obvious, and give a clear path from toy calls -> production integration.

Why different from existing onramps:
- Not a generic marketing page; a handhold-first quickstart for engineers (sample app + 3 CLI/SDK snippets that run in <2 minutes).
- Pricing transparency baked into the flow (cost estimator/preview before first call).
- Competitive differentiators frontloaded: predictable latency SLOs, model variant fallbacks, SDK-first streaming.

Core user journeys we want to support:
1) Fast evaluation: get a response from an example model in <2 minutes (curl + minimal SDK + runnable node/python example).
2) Bandwidth check: show median latency and tokens-for-sample so devs can estimate cost quickly.
3) Production readiness peek: link to Dedicated/Private options and SLA info for teams that want to escalate.

Launchpad building blocks (MVP):
- 1-click sandbox: creates API key with 1000 free tokens, pre-wired sample app in a reproducible environment (codesandbox/colab).
- Live cost preview widget: enter expected daily requests & avg tokens -> shows monthly estimate and cost buckets (hosted payg vs reserved commit).
- Example SDK patterns: streaming token handler, function-calling mock, embeddings/semantic search starter.
- Latency badge: small UI that shows typical median p95 for chosen model in your region.

Microcopy / headline experiments (3 variants):
Variant A (clarity-first):
- Headline: "Start generating in minutes — predictable cost, predictable latency."
- Subhead: "A single API, models tuned for production, and clear pricing so you can ship with confidence."

Variant B (developer-friendly casual):
- Headline: "Ship your first prompt in two minutes."
- Subhead: "Real latency numbers, sample apps, and an SDK that won't surprise you at scale."

Variant C (value-driven):
- Headline: "Production-ready inference without the ops overhead."
- Subhead: "Transparent per-token pricing, canary rollouts, and fallbacks when capacity matters."

Pricing-language hypotheses (for onramp + docs):
- Principle: make the unit of billing obvious and relatable. Avoid opaque compute units for the first pass; show tokens + an equivalent USD per 1k token rate for common models.
- Suggested short copy for pricing box: "Pay per token. Typical small responses cost ~$0.00X per 1k tokens. Estimate monthly cost using the preview widget."
- Experiment: show both per-1k-token and per-100-requests guidance for common patterns (chat greeting, document summary, embedding lookup).
- Reserved path CTAs: "Need predictable bills? Reserve capacity starting at X/month — we lock latency and unit price."

Pricing experiments to run (A/B):
1) Show hourly compute-minutes vs per-1k tokens (which yields more signups?).
2) Offer a small free token pool + 30-day dev credits vs immediate payg (which drives faster signups to prod?).
3) Show explicit debt: "Estimated monthly cost if you scale to 1M messages/day" — test whether a forward-looking example nudges enterprise inquiries.

Concise competitor notes (what to call out in messaging):
- OpenAI: strong brand familiarity and broad capabilities. Our angle: predictable latency SLOs, explicit rollback paths (model variants), and observability for token-level costs.
- Anthropic: safety/assistant-first positioning. Our angle: flexible deployment modes (hosted -> dedicated -> private) and lower variability when you need throughput.
- Cloud provider endpoints (GCP/Azure): easy infra bundling. Our angle: inference-tuned runtime and model profiles that reduce per-token compute; higher predictability and less ops.
- Replicate / small-hosted vendors: fast model access. Our angle: production controls, SLA options, and cost optimization tooling.

Quickstart snippets (micro, copy-ready):
- 1-line curl to show in the UI: curl https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{ "model": "rwd-1-mini", "prompt": "Hello from Redwood" }'
- Node SDK example (2–3 lines): const sdk = new Redwood({key: process.env.KEY}); await sdk.generate({model: 'rwd-1-mini', prompt: 'Summarize this: ...'});
- Embeddings starter: show sample of turning a query into vector and running a 10-doc cosine match. Keep pseudo-code short.

Questions / open decisions (for product + eng):
- Free token size for sandbox? 500, 1k, 5k? Tradeoff: more tokens -> deeper trial but higher abuse risk.
- Should latency badges derive from global averages or region+model-specific measurements? (prefer region-specific where available).
- What are the minimum telemetry hooks we expose in the UI to justify the "predictable" claim? (p95, median, token cost estimate)

KPIs to track for the experiment (suggested):
- Time-to-first-success (TFS): median time from sign-up -> first successful sample call (target < 3 minutes).
- Activation rate: % of signups that make >=5 API calls in first 7 days.
- Conversion to paid: % of sandbox users who become payg or commit in 30/90 days.
- Support requests about pricing: reduction expected if cost preview is clear.

Next steps (short roadmap):
- This week: align on microcopy variant and free token budget. Decide which metrics we can display as latency badge from existing telemetry.
- 2-week: implement 1-click sandbox + cost preview widget and wire three SDK examples.
- 4-week: run A/B with pricing microcopy variants + free credit sizes. Gather qualitative feedback from 10 developer interviews.

Notes to self / rough copy fragments:
- CTA button options: "Try Launchpad", "Run sample app", "Estimate my cost".
- Short FAQ piece: "How many tokens does a typical request use?" show 3 mini-examples (greeting, summarization, long-context).
- Observability hook: link to Console -> route-level cost breakdown after first 24 hours.

Raw brainstorm snippets (keep):
- "Badge: 35ms median (rwd-1-mini, us-west)" — build credibility.
- "Sandbox keys auto-expire after 30 days, convert seamlessly to production key" — lowers friction to escalate.
- "Preview budget slider in UI: slide daily calls -> see monthly estimate and percent of reserved threshold"

References / inspiration: internal onramp notes, developer survey Q3, SRE latency dashboards.

--end of draft--

Action: please review copy variants and pick 1 headline + 1 pricing format by Mon (Marshall to own A/B setup).
